newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Unichem still set on Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Unichem still set on Lloyds.

text.p: Pharmaceutical distribution and retail group Unichem Plc made clear on Wednesday that its sights were still set on taking over Lloyds Chemists Plc, but it wants to avoid a bidding war.
Its main rival for control of Lloyds, German wholesaler Gehe AG, said last month that it too was still interested in the retail chain once regulatory hurdles have been cleared.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, Unichem chief executive Jeff Harris said he did not want to get into an escalating price war. "I am concerned about that and we have got a clear idea of what value Lloyds might be to us," he said.

The Department of Trade and Industry ruled in July that both bids could go ahead as long as Gehe and Unichem find buyers for six Lloyds regional wholesaling businesses. German press reports on Wednesday suggested Gehe already had buyers lined up.
Harris said "there has been a lot of interest" in the sale, and he is optimistic the October 18 deadline will be met.

Unichem's agreed bid for Lloyds in January was topped by a 620-million-stg offer from Gehe before competition authorities stepped in. Unichem said costs of taking a 9.9 percent stake in Lloyds plus bid expenses pushed gearing to 52 percent by the end of June, compared to just four percent without the Lloyds bid.
Despite the pressure on borrowing, Unichem said first-half pretax profit rose 11.5 percent to 24.2 million pounds, and raised its interim dividend by 11.1 percent to 3.0 pence.

Harris said he remains convinced the acquisition of Lloyds is the right move for Unichem. But he said if it is thwarted Unichem "will continue to pursue the same strategy," targeting the UK's remaining 9,000 independent retail pharmacies and developing the fast-growing "pre-wholesale" business, taking on the internal delivery and supply operations of major companies.
Unichem has already won contracts with the UK arm of Bristol Myers Squibb Co and Smith & Nephew Plc
Unichem is part of a European-wide consortium for pre-wholesaling.
Harris saw the formation of a holding company and mergers as the way forward for the developing business.

The conventional wholesaling business was recovering from setbacks last year caused by poor customer service, with customers being won back and operating profit climbing 13 percent to 19.4 million stg, Harris said.
Retail operations, which include the Moss Chemists chain, saw profits improve 34 percent to 6.9 million stg. Harris said there is scope for further margin improvement at both divisions.
